_comment: Case-insensitive matching is decided per column. MySQL compares text case-insensitively everywhere, in unique keys too; PostgreSQL does not. citext lists the columns the code relies on being case-insensitive: text a person or an outside system typed or sent, which is looked up by equality or deduplicated by a unique key. caseSensitive lists unique-key text columns that are deliberately left case sensitive, each with the reason. Patterns may use * in the table or column part. The converter reports any other text column in a unique key as unaudited. Each site is re-checked by its parity test when it is converted.

caseSensitive.abtest.*: experiment labels written by the app in one fixed case
caseSensitive.authorities.area_code: Ordnance Survey area type codes, upper case
caseSensitive.aviva_votes.project: project labels written by the app
caseSensitive.azure_archive_copies.*: blob names and source labels, matched exactly
caseSensitive.batch_email_progress.job_type: job labels written by the app in one fixed case
caseSensitive.communityevents.externalid: an outside system's identifier, matched exactly
caseSensitive.config.key: settings keys written by the app in one fixed case
caseSensitive.cron_job_status.command: command names written by the scheduler
caseSensitive.email_digest_positions_daily.email_type: type labels written by the app in one fixed case
caseSensitive.firstreply_event_metrics.event: event labels written by the app in one fixed case
caseSensitive.groups_facebook*.*: Facebook identifiers; the Facebook integration is retired
caseSensitive.housekeeper_tasks.task_key: task keys written by the app in one fixed case
caseSensitive.item_desirability.model_version: model version labels written by the app

caseSensitive.mail_suppressed_counts.emailtype: type labels written by the app in one fixed case

caseSensitive.messages_desirability.model_version: model and prompt version labels written by the app
